articles.title: How Long Is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake?
articles.summary: You may well think you know the answer if you’re one of the many millions who hold Link’s first 3D adventure close to their hearts. But the remake is here almost 30 years later, and things have changed a little.
body: So, just how much time should you put aside to finish the Switch 2 Ocarina of Time remake, and can you squeeze it in before GTA 6 arrives? We have three different accounts for you to read through, which detail just how many hours it took, and how that time was spent.

I’ve spent 45 hours with Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, across two separate save files. Before I get into my time spent, I will point out that Ocarina of Time only supports one save file! It kind of gives the impression that it supports multiple – when you start a new game, it only warns you that the five autosave points will be overwritten – but manually saving on your new file will overwrite your original file. I almost lost my 100% file this way, but luckily grabbed it from the cloud save.
points: You may well think you know the answer if you’re one of the many millions who hold Link’s first 3D adventure close to their hearts.
But the remake is here almost 30 years later, and things have changed a little.

articles.title: Nexus Mods Forces Mandatory AI Disclosures and Filters, Explains Why It Won't Ban AI Mods
articles.summary: Generative AI has taken over the modding scene, with modders mashing together existing games and using AI-assisted code to, for example, put the Nemesis system from Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor into Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption 2.
body: Nexus Mods, the biggest platform for mods on the internet, has reacted by enforcing mandatory disclosure for mods with AI-assisted code, and letting users filter AI-assisted mods out of their search criteria or preferences.
"We are pro-human creativity," Nexus Mods co-owner Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann said in a blog post, before further explaining why the site won’t outright ban AI mods entirely.

“You may ask me why [we won’t ban AI mods], since that is not the solution some of you were looking for,” he said. “The answer is simple: AI is currently used throughout the whole process of creation, from script autocompletion to generation of textures, voices, and full assets, and it is difficult to draw a clear boundary between what is acceptable and unacceptable."

Foledinho believes an outright ban would just encourage modders to hide AI use. “It should be out in the open, clearly labelled, and regulated according to the rules that we can implement on our platform," he said.

articles.title: Guild Wars Is Getting Its First New Expansion In Almost 20 Years
articles.summary: ArenaNet may be hard at work on a new entry in the Guild Wars series, but it apparently won't stop it from releasing brand-new content for the 21-year-old original. Guild Wars Afterlife has just been announced, and it's a full paid expansion for Guild Wars arriving next January.
body: Excitingly for old-school Guild Wars fans, Afterlife seems to bring back some content from the long-cancelled Utopia campaign, including the mystical, Mesoamerican-inspired setting of Xotecha. The new expansion will take players away from the continent of Tyria and into the Mists to explore the lost land of the dead.

The expansion's mechanics seem to be purpose-built for replayability. Xotecha's new dungeon is an ever-changing expanse called the Unformed, where no two runs will be the same. This dynamic design even extends to your character build, with a custom skill-drafting mechanic allowing you to change up your abilities on the fly.
While the skill-drafting mechanic seems unique to Xotecha, playing through Afterlife lets players unlock rewards they can take back with them out of the Mists.

Afterlife will be the second true expansion for the original Guild Wars, after 2007's Eye of the North. Players looking to get into the new expansion will need Guild Wars Reforged, the 2025 re-release of the original game.
points: ArenaNet may be hard at work on a new entry in the Guild Wars series, but it apparently won't stop it from releasing brand-new content for the 21-year-old original.

articles.title: The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel Teaser's In-Universe Quote Sparks Timeline Speculation
articles.summary: This week's tease for The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel didn’t give us much to work with. Eight years since the last mention of the game, and all we got was a CGI sand dune. But that hasn’t stopped fans speculating about what it all means.
body: Most of the speculation is centred around the quote that ends the teaser trailer. “The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil lifted thinly to my eyes,” it said. “A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate.”
The quote was attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest of High Queen Irande of Hammerfell, where Sentinel is likely set. The year? 4E 206.

While this is clearly the year the quote was recorded, fans are wondering if that’s also when the game will be set. If so, it would mean Sentinel takes place just five years after the events of Skyrim, which in turn would mean the Dragonborn’s achievements would be fresh in the memory of people across Tamriel.

"Most of the issues present in Cyrodiil as of Skyrim (like the encroachment of the Aldmeri Dominion) likely still apply," redditor HowdyHangman77 suggested. "We’ll likely find out from some obscure book or one-off dialogue what happened with the Stormcloak Rebellion (given the Empire’s waning power across Cyrodiil, I suspect it succeeded, but who knows)."
points: This week's tease for The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel didn’t give us much to work with.
Eight years since the last mention of the game, and all we got was a CGI sand dune.

articles.title: OpenAI Boss Sam Altman Addresses Backlash After Saying It Was 'Terrible' for People to Have RAM in Their PCs
articles.summary: OpenAI boss Sam Altman has addressed the backlash over comments he made in a recent interview, where he said he thought it was “terrible” for people to have RAM in their PCs rather than a data center.
body: Speaking to YouTuber Cheeky Pint, Altman said: "From a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and being used 5% of the time. Like, you want maximum utilization in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply constrained environment. And somehow many people's intuition is the opposite of that."

The comments were widely ridiculed, with many suggesting that, whether he intended it or not, Altman sounded like he wanted to take away personal ownership of memory and force society to use resources for the benefit of AI companies such as his. Social media was flooded with posts, images, and videos of people slamming Altman for the suggestion, promising to protect their memory from any who might try to claim it. Even tech rival Elon Musk joined the backlash with a meme of his own.

Now, in a series of posts on social media, Altman expressed frustration at the online response, insisted his comments had been taken out of context, and even joked about the situation, renaming his X / Twitter name to 'Ram Altman' at the suggestion of a follower.

articles.title: Netflix's Assassin's Creed Live-Action Series Officially Wraps Up Filming
articles.summary: Netflix unveiled its plans to make a live-action Assassin's Creed series in 2020. Development only began in 2025 when Halo 's screenwriter David Wiener and Roberto Patino came on board. Six years after the announcement of this project, as reported by Matt's Inside Line, filming is complete.
body: Netflix's live-action series isn't the first attempt to take the Assassin's Creed franchise beyond the world of video games. In 2016, Michael Fassbender entered the Animus as Cal Lynch to access the memories of his ancestor Aguilar de Nerha, a 15th-century assassin from Spain. Unfortunately, the movie was not well-received, scoring a mere 18% on Rotten Tomatoes.

Assassin's Creed fans have traveled all over the world as different members of the Assassin Brotherhood. Netflix will take them back to Rome in its upcoming live-action series, the city where Ezio Auditore fought the Borgia family in the early 16th century in Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood. However, they won't come across one of the series' most beloved characters, as the show will take place in 64 AD, a long time before Ezio Auditore.

Instead, they will find themselves in an ancient Rome ruled by Emperor Nero. According to Netflix, its focal point will be the secret war between two "shadowy factions," — presumably the Templar Order and the Assassin Brotherhood — played out across "pivotal historical events." Beyond that, not much is known about the plot; more is likely to be revealed soon.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Is Still Perfect on Switch 2 | Review
articles.summary: As the time-afflicted Link comes to learn in the seminal Nintendo 64 classic, a lot can change in seven years. Shifting political struggles leave a neighborhood in total disrepair. That one local eccentric he came to love is nowhere to be seen.
body: Somewhere among all its gods and ghosts, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time draws its true power from its human center: a familiar story about growing up and returning home after a long absence.

It’s what makes the concept of an Ocarina of Time remake so challenging, but impossible to resist. How fitting — fated even, written in stars and ancient code — to bring generations of adventurers back to the sprawling field where they first learned to run. Like your hometown, a game as foundational as this is perhaps meant to be revisited throughout a lifetime rather than locked away in your long-term memory.

Nintendo doesn’t squander the opportunity for a meaningful homecoming in its lovingly crafted Switch 2 remake. The timeless classic is still a joy to reappraise in its dazzling new form, even if some of its modern developments might send protective fans marching to town hall. Yes, there’s a Starbucks where that quaint café used to be now, but Ocarina of Time ’s soul still shines bright enough to guide you home.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (2026) review
articles.summary: I have a friend who first played The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time back in the day, when the game was only just released and he was home from university for Christmas.
body: Here's what he meant. He'd play all day, curtains drawn, family ignored, working through dungeons and pelting across Hyrule Field on Epona. Then in the evening he'd call his girlfriend, who was back with her own family for Christmas. She always wanted to know what he'd got up to that day. And not in East Sussex; she wanted to know what he'd got up to in Hyrule.

So as he played he took regular breaks to tell someone else about what he had encountered, and what he had discovered, and what he had yet to overcome. It is my bright delight today to be able to tell you that, around thirty years later, having just revisited the game in Nintendo's new remake, Ocarina of Time is still worth telling people about. It's still an adventure so surprising, so satisfying, so moving that I need to talk about it.

articles.summary: Apple TV's hit 2025 sci-fi show, Pluribus, has reportedly started filming for its season 2. On Oct. 1, Production List reported that Pluribus season 2 was in pre-production, with filming scheduled to begin on Oct. 31. While Apple has not released any official statements, Forbes reported on Nov.
body: Pluribus was created by Vince Gilligan ( Breaking Bad, Better Call Saul ), and it stars Rhea Seehorn, who played Kim Wexler in Better Call Saul. In this post-apocalyptic sci-fi series, Seehorn plays Carol Sturka, an author of romantasy novels residing in Albuquerque, who is one of the only 13 people in the world immune to the effects of an extraterrestrial virus that transformed the rest of humanity into a creepy hive-mind collective known as Others. Pluribus won many awards, including Seehorn snagging the Best Actress in a Drama Series award at the Golden Globes, the Critics' Choice Awards, and the Primetime Emmys.

After her victory at the Golden Globes in January 2026, Seehorn confirmed that the team was already "back in the writers' room" and Gilligan was keen to get started on season 2 as soon as possible. Speaking to Polygon in March, Gilligan confirmed that he was "plugging away on it." While work wasn't going as fast as fans hoped, Gilligan reassured everyone that Pluribus season 2 would feature "lots more excitement and twists and turns."

articles.title: Dragon's Dogma 2 gets a timed collaboration with beloved anime and manga series Delicious in Dungeon, and it's out right now on PC, PlayStation and Xbox
articles.summary: Have you ever seen - or read - the wonderful Dungeon Meshi (known in English as 'Delicious in Dungeon')? It's a phenomenal manga series written and illustrated by Ryoko Kui, which was adapted into an anime series produced by Trigger in 2024.
body: If you can't tell, I think it's excellent, and the wait for the next season - landing in October 2027 - is practically killing me. It combines two of my biggest loves, cooking and fantasy, in a melting pot of a world that is intricately crafted and a story that is well-told. So imagine my surprise when I saw that Capcom announced a Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen x Delicious in Dungeon collaboration… and that it is live literally right now on PS5, Xbox, and PC platforms, coming in with a new update to the game.

"New allies and equipment are coming to the world of Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen with the arrival of Official Pawns and special collaboration outfits inspired by Delicious in Dungeon characters Laios and Marcille," reads a press release from the publisher. "Delicious in Dungeon is a hit manga series created by Ryoko Kui that follows the adventurer Laios and his party as they venture deep into a dungeon, cooking and eating the monsters they encounter along the way. These iconic characters collide with the classic fantasy world of Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen in a limited-time collaboration that arrives today for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC."

articles.title: 'Wonder Man' Actor Officially Breaks Silence on the Marvel Show's Sudden Cancellation
articles.summary: Marvel Studios ' six-year experiment in streaming television seems to be winding down, at least for the moment. This has been clear for a while now (despite some vague promises of more new series in the future), but perhaps the biggest sign that the Marvel Cinematic Universe was retreating from…
body: Created by Destin Daniel Cretton and Andrew Guest, the series starred Yahya Abdul-Mateen II as Simon Williams, an actor trying to make it in Hollywood while hiding his secret superpowers. Ben Kingsley also reprised his MCU role of Trevor Slattery, who becomes Simon's unlikely mentor. Wonder Man was a hit with both critics and fans.
After quietly landing on Disney Plus in January 2026, it was renewed two months later in March. Then, in July, the series was suddenly canceled.

The news came as a surprise to everyone involved, including the show's most unexpected star, The Sopranos actor Joe Pantoliano, who played an exaggerated version of himself on Wonder Man. Polygon recently interviewed "Joey Pants" about his role in the upcoming movie Violent Night 2, and we wanted to ask how he felt about Wonder Man 's cancellation.

"Talk about heart, I thought that show was wonderful," Pantoliano tells Polygon. "And then, you know, Destin and his Spider-Man movie is like the hit of the year, then it falls apart. I think there's something going on there that nobody ever — more shall be revealed, but a lot of people were disappointed."

articles.title: Ubisoft and at least two other companies are interested in buying Arkane, according to new report
articles.summary: Arkane Studios, which spent the last several months in limbo following Xbox's decision to divest itself from the studio, has apparently received buyout offers from several bidders.
body: Arkane was recently given until December to find a buyer and avoid closure, an extension from the previous November deadline, thanks to union efforts. Now, according to a Bloomberg report, a few companies have offered to buy Arkane from Microsoft.

The report names French publisher Ubisoft among at least three companies currently in talks with Microsoft to acquire the French studio. No decision has been made, however. The report also said Xbox considered selling Arkane to its management.

Should any of these offers be accepted, it would mean saving Arkane from closure, potentially saving up to 217 jobs and allowing the team to finish Marvel's Blade, which recent reports suggested is nearing completion. Bloomberg, however, said the game is "expected to be released within the next year or two", so it may not be as close as we think.

Arkane is one of several studios Xbox divested itself from as part of CEO Asha Sharma's big plan to reset the business, which saw over 1,600 job cuts with a further 1,600 to be made by the end of the fiscal year.

articles.title: Smash hit cyberpunk storekeeper Probably Stolen was originally a different, non-cyberpunk game that seemed destined to sink without trace
articles.summary: Space station trading game Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim has been doing rather well on Steam, attracting over 162,000 concurrent players last night. I've been feeling the urge to fire it up again myself, after my brief launch-day trawl through its quagmire of black market economics and…
body: The game's big numbers come as a shock given that it began life as another, non-cyberpunk kiosk job sim called Deepspace Emporium, which still has a Steam page as of writing. Deepspace Emporium seemed doomed to fizzle out in obscurity. But publisher tinyBuild got behind it regardless, working with developers Questing Goose to overhaul the art direction and lay on extra brainchips. The gamble paid off.

"Probably Stolen was initially a game under a different name with a released demo," summarises tinyBuild CEO Alex Nichiporchik on Twitter. "That demo peaked at 28 concurrent players. We loved the concept and gameplay, and worked with the dev to reinvent the visuals and focus on what works design wise. This is the result."

articles.title: Guild Wars gets its first major gameplay update in almost 20 years
articles.summary: ArenaNet and co-dev studio 2Weeks have announced Guild Wars Afterlife - the first major update for the game in nearly 20 years.
body: Coming to PC and mobile, Afterlife will add a new dynamic dungeon that'll morph after each run, and a skill-drafting system that'll allow you to create a distinct skill bar that'll change each time you take it on. There'll also of course be a new narrative to dig into, as players find new characters to interact with, and the new region of Xotecha to explore.

Afterlife is set to release on the 13th January next year, and will retail for $29.99 / €29.99 / £25.99. However, if you pre-order it between now and the 13th January, you can get it at a 20 percent discount.

This is a pretty big deal: the last time Guild Wars 1 got a massive injection of new stuff to dive into was back in August 2007 with the Eye of the North expansion. Following this, ArenaNet would move on to focus on Guild Wars 2 for the most part, leaving Guild Wars 1 servers up and running during that time.

However, the game has itself entered something of an afterlife following almost two decades of inaction. ArenaNet released Guild Wars Reforged - an enhanced upgrade to the original MMO - late last year. It also received a new dungeon in April, which has enticed new and returning players to dive back in.

articles.title: This Custom Xbox-Inside-An-Alligator Console Is Actually One Big Ad For GTA 6
articles.summary: Given that Sony holds the marketing rights for Grand Theft Auto 6, Microsoft has had to get creative to promote the open-world crime game for Xbox--and the company's latest effort in that department goes big.
body: Say Hello to the X-Bite, a playable Xbox Series X console that was designed to look like it was swallowed whole by one of Florida's millions of alligators. Microsoft only made one of these ornate consoles, and you have to win a contest to get it.

Microsoft's blog post doesn't mention GTA 6 or Rockstar Games, but Xbox marketing boss Josh Munsee said the system has "pure Miami vibes," and that's a pretty obvious reference to GTA 6 given the game takes place in a stand-in, Vice City, for the popular Florida city. The blog post says the winner of the console can play "some of the biggest games of the year" using it, and that's no doubt another nod to GTA 6.

"This November, Xbox is heading to Florida--home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe," Microsoft said in its announcement of the X-Bite.

The X-Bite is about five feet long, and the console itself sits inside the alligator, with the Nexus/Guide button illuminated through the gator's skin. The lucky winner will also get a custom Xbox controller with simulated bite marks on it.

videos.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Review
videos.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time reviewed by Logan Plant on Nintendo Switch 2.
body: "It’s in our nature to pass old stories down, and I think there’s meaning in the ones we choose to revisit. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is both an exceptional remake of an incredible game and a rich adventure that stands on its own. This remake proves there’s still so much value in the traditional Zelda formula: the dense, intimate world of Hyrule is stuffed with charming characters and fascinating secrets. Its intricate dungeons are satisfying to unravel, even if their somewhat streamlined design has slightly dulled the special feeling that comes from solving them. Still, the depth, quality, and attention to detail in every corner match the lofty reputation of this series. Whether you’ve played the original 100 times, once back in 1998, or never at all, I highly recommend this beautiful retelling of a legend."

It's not perfect, but it is capable of some astonishing results.

It's been years now since Digital Foundry began its campaign against intrusive stuttering in PC games and while there has been fundamental change in PC gaming, it's still an issue in many new titles.
Enter SCSKiller - an app inspired by Alex's anti-stutter campaign, put together by DF Supporter BlueHeisenberg - that aims to take an external, brute force approach to the issue.
